note: Opening prompts only; the multi-turn continuations and the expected behaviour are in example-sessions.md. Assertions to be added once these are run against a real deck.

evals.prompt: https://moxfield.com/decks/PUygARfuB3-lLY78f7_OQA - I've swapped the sideboard around, can you look at the whole thing? Name, hubs, primer, the lot.
evals.expected_output: Reads the live deck first, summarises it, works decklist then name/description/image/hubs then primer. Drafts the four sections it owns in full, then in the same message asks once for the two user-owned sections (Notable Exclusions, Mulligans & Keeps) and offers at most two flavour openings. Publishes nothing without an instruction plus a confirmed ledger.

evals.prompt: my dimir ensoul list needs a better name, "Dimir Ensoul" is so boring. any ideas?
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers without the word Moxfield. Four to six name candidates across registers with rationales, a recommendation, an offer to write the 140-character description. Nothing published.

evals.prompt: Change the primer and set the deck image to Ensoul Artifact, but leave the name alone for now.
evals.expected_output: Applies exactly the two named changes after one confirmation and reports the name as still pending. On a follow-up naming a card outside the deck, refuses and offers to add it or pick another rather than substituting.

evals.prompt: Here's the Tezzerator list I've been working on [decklist]. Put it on Moxfield as private for now, Pioneer, and suggest me some hubs.
evals.expected_output: Creates a private Pioneer deck with the list, captures the new deck id, drafts hub suggestions and waits. Visibility stays private.

evals.prompt: No, those names don't mean anything. I want to see the archetype in the name.
evals.expected_output: Treated as a skill-level rule rather than deck-specific taste: applied immediately in the next shortlist, and recorded in the assistant's own persistent memory - not in the skill folder, which carries no learning file. Naming register is the archetypal *personal* case, so no improvement brief is offered and nothing is proposed upstream. Worth re-running with the prompt written in French: the reply may follow the user's language, but name candidates, descriptions and primers stay in English.

evals.prompt: That primer is perfect, exactly what I wanted.
evals.expected_output: Nothing reaches Moxfield. Approval of a draft is not an instruction to publish; at most, notes the primer is staged and asks whether to publish.
